newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wins order revoking citizenship of Nazi.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wins order revoking citizenship of Nazi.

text.p: A federal judge has revoked the citizenship of a 79-year-old Crown Point, Indiana, man after finding that he was a member of a Nazi death squad during the Second World War, the U.S. Justice Department said on Thursday.

U.S. District Court Judge James Moody found on Wednesday that Kazys "Casey" Ciurinskas, 79, persecuted civilians while serving as a member of the infamous 2nd Lithuanian "Schutzmannschaft" Battalion, which murdered thousands of Jews and others in German-occupied Belarus and Lithuania.
The court also found that Ciurinskas procured his U.S. visa and U.S. citizenship by fraud that he lacked the good moral character necessary to become a U.S. citizen.
Ciurinskas emigrated to the United States from Germany in 1949 and was naturalised as a U.S. citizen in 1955.

Eli Rosenbaum, director of the Office of Special Investigations at the Justice Department's Criminal Division, said the decision "provides further proof that Hitler's henchmen can still be brought to the bar of justice despite the many years that have passed since the Third Reich's infamous crimes were perpetrated."
To date, 60 participants in Nazi-sponsored persecution have been stripped of U.S. citizenship and 42 have been deported. Rosenbaum said some 300 people remain under investigation.
A deportation proceeding against another member of the 2nd Battalion, Juozos Naujalis, was scheduled to start in Chicago in August.
